# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 53 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 53 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_053_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 4 — Trees in Summer: The Age to Come Reveals the Difference

**53:1** He showed me many trees, some budding and some withered. And he said to me: "Do you see these trees?" "I see them, lord," I said; "some are budding and some are withered." "Those that are budding," he said, "are the righteous who are to dwell in the age to come; for the age to come is summer for the righteous, but winter for the sinners.

**53:2** When therefore the mercy of the Lord shines forth, then those who serve God shall be made manifest, and all men shall be made manifest. For as in summer the fruit of every tree is made manifest, and all become known what they are — so also the fruit of the righteous shall be made manifest, and they all shall be made known who have been flourishing in that age.

**53:3** But the Gentiles and sinners — as you saw the dry trees — such shall they be found, dry and without fruit in that age, and they shall be burned as wood for fuel and shall be made manifest, because their practice in their lives was evil. For the sinners shall be burned, because they sinned and did not repent. And the Gentiles shall be burned because they did not know the one who created them.

**53:4** Bear fruit therefore yourself, so that your fruit may be made manifest in that summer. And do not be much occupied with business and mix yourself up with wealth of every kind, but rather practice holiness, so that you may be prepared for the summer and not be found withered. For all that are occupied with business and with wealth shall be withered in that age, unless they are found bearing fruit."

---

*EMET renders the Greek of P.Mich. 130 with maximal literalness, preserving the summer/winter eschatological contrast of Similitude 4.*
